name: What permits are needed for triplex construction in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: Which permits and approvals usually come before building a triplex in Los Angeles, Pasadena, Glendale, or Burbank?
mainEntity.text: Which permits and approvals usually come before building a triplex in Los Angeles, Pasadena, Glendale, or Burbank?

acceptedAnswer.text: A triplex usually involves multiple layers of approval, not just a building permit. The project may need zoning confirmation, planning review, architectural and structural plan check, demolition permits, grading permits, sewer or utility approvals, and final building permits. Some sites also trigger additional review for fire access, driveway design, trees, drainage, or special overlays. The permit sequence matters because missing one required approval can delay the whole project. Owners should treat permitting as a coordinated process rather than a single filing event. The smoothest projects start with a complete feasibility review, then move into drawings that anticipate local plan check expectations. That approach reduces redesign, saves time, and lowers the chance of expensive corrections later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Triplex projects typically require zoning review, plan check, building permits, and often additional approvals for demolition, grading, utilities, and fire access. Depending on the site, there may also be separate review for planning, landscaping, and engineering. The exact permit path depends on the city and parcel conditions.
